# Machine-owned mission

The user explicitly requires the machine itself to rebuild the machinery and
perform the mathematical campaigns. The supervisor supplies requirements,
resource boundaries, primary-paper identities, independent review, and versioning;
it must not supply mathematical answers or prewritten proof recipes.

## Construction

Read docs/DESIGN.md in full. Starting from this empty project, implement the
research system and its formal foundations. The actual proposer is Codex with
gpt-6-astra. Develop executable code, not just an architectural report. Keep
problem contracts explicit, and separate mathematical truth from usefulness
and novelty. There are no artificial research levels or lemma-count rewards.
Kolmogorov/description-length measures are audit-only and may not affect
curiosity, scheduling, admission, or switch approval.

The action space must support literature search, Python/Sage/GAP experiments
when available, representation changes, conjectures, Lean proofs/refutations,
component gluing, and proposed code changes. Unavailable tools are capability
failures. Experiments and retrieved text are not Lean theorems. Provisional
exploration remains flexible; persistent certified self-rewrites require the
whole-continuation proof, an operational connection, exact bindings, and costs.

Construct and test the proof-admission boundary and the reflective execution
model. Formally define the gluing maps and prove the preservation properties
actually used. Demonstrate a concrete installed self-rewrite tied to its checked
semantics. Explicitly report model assumptions and implementation limits.
Do not call a benchmark improvement, abstract implication, changed prompt, or
untested gate a full Gödel machine. Never introduce sorry, admissions, hidden
axioms, native-evaluation axioms, or a postulated global self-soundness theorem.
Use ordinary Mathlib axioms only, and independently audit English versus Lean.

## First mathematical campaign

Takashi Agoh, An Intrinsic Factor of an Alternating Sum Involving Certain
Rational Functions, INTEGERS 26 (2026), A9.
Primary paper: https://math.colgate.edu/~integers/aa9/aa9.pdf
DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.18154119

Retrieve the original source, inventory its statements and hypotheses, choose
and formalize the paper exercise through the machine's own agenda, reproduce
the relevant proofs or rigorously identify errors, and audit statement meaning.
Record what has and has not been established. Do not replace universal claims
with finite scans or silently change their hypotheses.

## Subsequent conjecture campaign

S. J. Evans, A. P. Veselov, B. Winn, Arithmetic and Geometry of Markov polynomials.
Primary paper: https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.14882
Publisher: https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html
Target: Conjecture 6.3, coefficient log-concavity of Markov polynomials.

After the first campaign, attack this conjecture using the rebuilt machine.
Read and audit the exact target before formalizing it. The machine chooses its
own lemmas, representations, literature, experiments, and proof attempts.
The aim is a serious, reproducible attack, not an invented claim of resolution.

## Provenance and workflow

All generated code, proofs, and experiments must carry machine provenance.
Use short, durable checkpoints so interruption does not erase work. Preserve
failed attempts and explicit remaining obligations. The supervisor will make
local Git commits; do not read or modify Git internals, push, or contact people.
Remain inside this project and the supplied third-party toolchain/dependencies.
Do not read older project archives, previous-session transcripts, retired build
outputs, or predecessor proofs. No solution from an earlier version is supplied.
# Clean bootstrap of a Gödel machine for mathematical research

This document is a design specification for a fresh construction. It supplies
no previous implementation, mathematical results, proof scripts, or successful
research strategies. It distinguishes an adaptive mathematical researcher, a
formally certified continuation model, and an executable Gödel machine. A
checked theorem about an abstract model does not by itself establish that an
implementation realizes that model or that the model describes future Astra
calls.

The intended system uses a flexible LLM proposer, reusable mathematical
components, and explicit gluing interfaces. It can search literature, conduct
computational experiments, change representations, formulate conjectures, and
attempt proofs and refutations. Its scientific objective is problem-specific.
Kolmogorov-style measurements are audit data, not a universal objective or an
automatic curiosity reward.

## What the original construction requires

Schmidhuber's target compares a proposed switch with continuing the entire
incumbent program, including future proof search and later self-modifications.
The machine and environment are axiomatized. Checking and installation take
time; the switch protocol binds a target time and can reject a late proof.
The resulting optimality claim is relative to the utility, assumptions, and
incumbent search, rather than an oracle maximum over all programs. The paper
also permits a nondegradation target, different initial searchers, and changes
to utility code justified by the previous utility. Its mathematical example
rewards the first verified proof or disproof by the reciprocal of elapsed time.
Useful changes may be unprovable in the chosen system or undiscoverable within
available resources. These requirements come from §§2.4, 3.2, 4, 5, and 6 of
[the original paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0309048).

The architecture and acceptance criteria below are our engineering proposal.
They are not claims that the original paper supplies a working implementation
for Lean, an opaque external LLM, or this mathematical research problem.

## The problem contract, rather than manufactured levels

ARC supplies an external environment with explicit levels and validated
completion conditions. The mathematics application has no corresponding
natural sequence of levels. Numbering accepted lemmas does not create one.

A run therefore starts with an explicit, versioned problem contract:

- An exact root proposition, its intended English meaning, and permitted
  assumptions. Resolution may mean a checked proof or checked negation.
- A declared utility or preference over research outcomes and their costs.
  This is supplied for the problem, not inferred from a theorem counter.
- Resource limits and a cost interpretation: abstract computation steps,
  elapsed time, provider usage, or separately recorded quantities.
- The environment assumptions under which prospective comparisons are made.
- Admission and completion rules that a proposal cannot redefine.

A root-resolution/time objective is one reasonable instance, not a default
definition of all mathematical value. Intermediate results can have value
when the contract says how that value is assessed. If such an assessment is
human or heuristic, its status must remain visible.

Truth, relevance, novelty, and expected usefulness are separate properties.
A kernel-checked lemma establishes its proposition. A separately checked
reduction can establish its logical connection to the root. Neither fact
alone establishes historical novelty or how likely the lemma is to help.
Even an implication into the root can have an impossible antecedent.
Experimental evidence may change the agenda without closing a formal task.

No part of admission, root closure, scheduling, or persistent rewrite approval
may quietly depend on source length, compression ratio, or a claimed estimate
of Kolmogorov complexity. Audit measurements can still describe reuse and
representation costs. Their production must have ordinary resource accounting.

## Open research actions and explicit evidence

The proposer needs an extensible action interface rather than a fixed menu of
prewritten mathematical recipes. Concrete capabilities can include:

| Action | Output | What the output establishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Literature search and source reading | Queries, primary URLs, passages, retrieval times | What a source reports; not a Lean theorem |
| Python, Sage, or GAP experiment | Program, inputs, versions, outputs, costs | A reproducible computation under recorded semantics |
| Representation proposal | Definitions, maps, examples, desired transport laws | A proposed viewpoint until its laws are checked |
| Proof or refutation | Exact target, proof term, dependencies, kernel receipt | The proposition admitted by the proof gate |
| Component attachment | Boundary, bindings, adapters, checked obligations | The specific preservation properties proved |
| Search strategy proposal | Diagnosis, next actions, resource allocation | Provisional guidance consumed by the controller |
| Persistent code rewrite | Exact replacement, state migration, switch certificate | Only the certified comparison and preservation claims |

An adapter may expose a new experimental language or mathematical interface
without giving the proposer unrestricted host authority. The broker enforces
capabilities and records failures. An unavailable Sage or GAP installation is
a capability failure, not evidence against a conjecture. Network failures,
timeouts, and malformed responses similarly remain transport or execution
outcomes rather than mathematical refutations.

Finite scans do not prove universal claims. Exact counterexamples can become
formal refutations after the relevant witness and hypotheses are independently
checked. External theorems may be recorded as explicit assumptions when a
contract permits that treatment; retrieved text must not add hidden axioms.

## Exploration must not require a switch proof at every step

The incumbent research policy may already authorize broad exploratory actions,
task invention, hypothesis changes recorded as new tasks, and provisional
strategy updates. Choosing such an action is ordinary execution of that policy.
It need not first prove that its next web query or experiment is globally best.

A persistent replacement of the controller or its search procedure is a
different event. It requires either the full switch gate described below or an
explicitly labeled experimental branch that makes no certified-improvement
claim. Successful tests alone must not promote that branch to a proved switch.

This separation prevents two failures: an inert system unable to explore until
it has solved its own research problem, and an unrestricted self-editor whose
ordinary strategy changes are advertised as Gödel-certified improvements.
Exploration remains flexible within the current contract and capability limits.

## Operational semantics and the whole continuation

The formal machine state should contain executable controller and proof-search
code, persistent research data, the archive and agenda, resource state, pending
requests, and enough environment history to interpret future actions. Program
code must be inspectable data. A semantics must explain how each instruction,
external response, and accepted rewrite changes that state.

Crucially, the incumbent continuation includes its own future proposals,
verification attempts, discoveries, and switches. A comparison against a
frozen policy that is forbidden to improve does not compare against the actual
incumbent. The replacement continuation must likewise include its subsequent
behavior, not just its first apparently beneficial action.

One conceptual interface is:

```text
step       : Program × State × Input -> Transition
run        : Program × State × Environment -> Trace
evaluate   : ProblemContract × Trace -> Utility
install    : Candidate × State -> InstallationTrace × State
```

This interface is a specification sketch, not an executable API or a proof.
In a stochastic instance, `run` induces a distribution and `evaluate` supplies
an expected value when the required measurability and integrability hold.
In a robust instance, comparisons quantify over declared environment behaviors.
The implementation must connect these objects to the bytes it actually runs.

## The switch obligation and a common time baseline

For contract `C`, model `mu`, incumbent `p`, candidate `q`, and decision state
`s`, the intended strict obligation is:

```text
V(C, mu, install-and-continue(q, s))
  > V(C, mu, continue-whole-machine(p, s)).
```

Both sides use the same contract, environmental assumptions, and decision
baseline. The comparison may instead be nonstrict when that is the declared
rule. This is a semantic statement about complete continuations; it is not a
claim that both values must be computed exactly before a proof can be found.

Search already performed before this baseline is sunk on both branches. Do not
charge it twice or selectively subtract it from the incumbent. Validation and
installation still to be performed must be included. If final validation has
already occurred, its elapsed time instead appears in the new state and the
remaining lifetime. A certificate proved from an earlier snapshot must justify
transport to the installation state or be checked against an appropriate future
deadline and invariant. Simply adding a measured cost to an old inequality is
insufficient when the remaining opportunity to solve the problem has changed.

A switch receipt must bind the contract and model, incumbent and replacement
code, exact state or proved state invariant, migration, cost interpretation,
deadline, certificate target, and independent verification artifacts. Reject
changed bindings and stale deadlines. Hashes bind recorded bytes; they are not
proofs that Python or operating-system execution realizes the Lean semantics.

Changing runtime reward code cannot redefine the standard used to approve the
change. Representation changes to the objective require a transport proof.
A new scientific objective requires a new explicit contract; silently weakening
the root or environmental assumptions is not an improvement.

## Opaque models and self-reference

Astra is an external proposer with unknown internals and no assumed success
probability. Treat its responses and delays as environmental inputs. A measured
acceptance rate, benchmark gain, or confidence estimate does not establish its
future response law. A Bayesian comparison is conditional on its declared
model; a robust comparison must actually quantify over the stated model class.
Neither should be reported as an unconditional real-world guarantee.

One promising certificate pattern proves preservation for every corresponding
response stream while reducing internal work. However, corresponding streams
require justification: an API or web service can depend on request time and
history. Faster execution need not receive the same responses. The environment
contract or a coupling argument must support that correspondence.

Encoding one's own code is not the same as proving unrestricted soundness of
one's own proof system. A sufficiently strong consistent theory cannot simply
adopt its own unrestricted reflection principle. This is the relevant obstacle
discussed in [Yudkowsky and Herreshoff's primary analysis](https://intelligence.org/files/TilingAgentsDraft.pdf).
Our design uses particular checked proofs and concrete simulations; it must
not introduce an unchecked `SelfSound` axiom to discharge future correctness.
The reference kernel, admission semantics, and runtime bridge are explicit
trust boundaries. Faster implementations need preservation certificates against
that reference; replacing the reference by a candidate's assertion of trust
does not prove preservation.

## Gluing and representation transport

A finite-name attachment can have a unique-extension property for compatible
maps. Proving such a restricted pushout would not establish semantic
conservativity of arbitrary source edits or dependent Lean declarations.

The design requires typed interfaces: declarations, hypotheses, dependencies,
interpretations, and any renaming or substitution. A new cell must discharge
its assumptions from the accepted context. Context attachment should preserve
the original models and hence their consequences. Sequential attachment must
preserve this fact, including when later cells reuse earlier checked cells.

A representation adapter must preserve the observations or predicates needed
by its consumer. When a representation identifies two objects that a target
property distinguishes, no exact adapter can recover that property from the
representation alone. Such collisions should become explicit failed obligations
or counterexamples, not be hidden by successful tests on a small sample.

For code components, coherent signatures are only the beginning: a simulation
must connect glued implementations to their specification and cost model.
Gluing correctness then supports a switch proof; it does not imply usefulness.
The terms “cofibered” and “cofibrant” require a specified category, structure,
and associated laws. Fiber-respecting maps and injective context embeddings
alone do not establish a model-category cofibration or a Grothendieck opfibration.

## Milestones and acceptance criteria

1. **Problem-directed exploration.** Run the configurable contract and action
   broker with Astra proposals, real feedback, explicit evidence classes, and
   cost accounting. Demonstrate a nonproof action affecting a later research
   decision. Synthetic fixtures test the protocol; they do not demonstrate
   autonomous mathematical discovery.
2. **Semantic foundations.** Prove conservative context attachment, representation
   transport conditions, and continuation comparisons with explicit costs.
   A bounded trace/Bellman model is a useful verified instance. State exactly
   which horizon, response relation, and policy class it quantifies over.
3. **Reflective executable bridge.** Provide executable code semantics with code
   in state and future switching included. Prove or explicitly audit the bridge
   from concrete controller transitions, time accounting, and state migration
   to that semantics. Merely supplying an arbitrary value function fails this
   milestone. A finite table or a single prescribed trajectory also fails it.
4. **A concrete certified self-change.** Produce a candidate, an independently
   checked whole-continuation certificate, and an actual guarded installation.
   A semantics-preserving optimization with a net cost improvement is a useful
   first case. Its proof must cover future switches and installation overhead,
   not merely reproduce the outcomes in the selection benchmark.
5. **General search and reuse.** Let the proposer invent components, adapters,
   and candidate rewrites. A fair proof enumerator can supply completeness
   relative to a calculus if required; an LLM alone supplies no such guarantee.
   Neither option requires a Kolmogorov reward or manufactured task levels.

Completing a finite, specified instance does not establish a switch guarantee
for arbitrary unbounded research or an unmodeled LLM. A generic theorem whose
hypotheses assume the very utility comparison at issue is a framework, not an
independent proof that a concrete rewrite improves the researcher.

## Adversarial examples and regression requirements

The audit must include passing examples and failures with one condition removed:

- A valid reduction versus an unrelated true lemma falsely credited as root
  completion; a refutation of the exact goal versus a changed-hypothesis target.
- A numerical pattern versus a kernel-checked universal statement; a missing
  experimental tool versus a negative mathematical result.
- A compatible attachment versus a conflicting binding, new unproved assumption,
  omitted dependency, circular cell dependency, or lossy representation adapter.
- A cheaper equivalent continuation versus one whose installation overhead
  removes the gain, or whose earlier deadline defeats the promised outcome.
- A full incumbent that later finds a better rewrite versus a comparator that
  artificially disables that future search; the latter certificate must fail.
- Identical objective semantics versus a replacement that edits the reward,
  root, model assumptions, or verifier to manufacture apparent improvement.
- A correctly bound certificate versus changed candidate bytes, changed state,
  stale time, mismatched model, forged receipt, or replayed old approval.
- An exploratory strategy revision versus a persistent executable rewrite;
  exploratory authorization must not silently authorize the latter.
- Different complexity-audit values with identical research inputs: admission,
  scheduling, and switch decisions remain identical. Logging costs may differ
  only when the measurement operation itself genuinely differs.

Formal negative examples should exhibit the missing mathematical hypothesis,
not just malformed JSON. Runtime tests should exercise actual gate boundaries.
Successful tests are evidence about implementation behavior, not a substitute
for the semantic connection required by milestone 3.

## Machine-authored bootstrap and experimental status

The initial input is this design, the user-selected research problem descriptions
and primary-source references, pinned Lean/Mathlib metadata, and a minimal launch
and containment interface. The machine must create the new implementation,
formal statements, proofs, experiments, tests, and documentation. The supervisor
provides execution, resource limits, evidence retention, and independent audit;
it must not insert mathematical solution steps or implement the research engine
on the machine's behalf while describing the result as machine-authored.

A bootstrap cannot claim that its first controller edits are already authorized
by a Gödel switch theorem whose verifier and executable semantics it has yet to
construct. Those edits run in an explicitly experimental workspace under the
user's authorization to rebuild. Compilation, tests, and subsequent independent
checks can validate aspects of the resulting code. They do not retroactively
prove that the bootstrap's sequence of edits was utility-optimal.

The machine must report separate transitions between these statuses:

- **Experimental bootstrap:** code generation and exploration without an
  installed whole-continuation switch certificate.
- **Checked research:** concrete proof objects pass an independently validated
  admission boundary; individual accepted propositions may be reported exactly.
- **Verified model:** formal theorems describe an explicitly stated machine and
  environment model, with the implementation bridge still separately identified.
- **Certified persistent switch:** an actual installation passes the bound,
  independently checked certificate and execution-bridge obligations above.

These labels are evidence classes, not mathematical levels, utility scores,
or a requirement that all components progress in a fixed order. A machine can
produce a valid mathematical theorem during an experimental bootstrap. That
alone certifies neither its surrounding engine nor its future self-modifications.
Machine-generated reports of success remain claims until their evidence is
independently checked; a self-authored test harness cannot certify itself by
printing a successful receipt.

## Clean-input and provenance acceptance checklist

Before the rebuilding proposer runs, independently verify the following:

- Historical source, draft implementations, proof scripts, discoveries, tests,
  experiments, transcripts, and run receipts are archived for the user outside
  the proposer's readable filesystem boundary. They are not bootstrap inputs.
- A Git archive preserves the historical work without exposing its object store
  or archive branch to the proposer. Deleting the working tree while leaving
  `git show` access to earlier solutions does not establish a clean boundary.
- No historical project `.olean`, generated module, cached proof expression,
  database, notebook output, or task-specific package supplies previous results.
  A pinned standard Lean/Mathlib installation is a declared dependency, not
  evidence of a newly created theorem.
- The proposer begins with a fresh conversation. Old assistant summaries,
  hidden solution files, previous success reports, and strategy suggestions
  are not inherited through its prompt, tools, environment, or resume state.
- Task inputs identify the selected publication or conjecture and the required
  outcome. They do not include previously found witnesses, lemmas, reductions,
  or successful representations. Public primary sources remain legitimate
  research inputs and their actual use is recorded.
- The run records an input manifest, hashes, toolchain pins, capabilities,
  workspace boundary, initial prompt, model identity, and resource limits.
  Archived historical objects and fresh generated objects remain distinguishable.
- All new code and mathematical artifacts are traceable to machine actions.
  Any later human correction, imported result, or boundary exception is recorded
  explicitly and narrows the corresponding autonomy or clean-input claim.
- Generated artifacts cannot overwrite supervisor-owned launch rules, hidden
  archives, independent validation tools, evidence manifests, or contract inputs.
  Proposed changes to those components remain candidates for separate review.

A prompt requesting that the proposer ignore readable historical answers is a
behavioral instruction, not enforced clean isolation. If filesystem isolation
is unavailable, report that limitation rather than claiming an enforced clean
run. The archive must remain recoverable by the user; cleaning the proposer
workspace does not authorize loss of the preserved historical work.

## What this specification does not yet establish

No implementation, kernel-checked result, certified controller rewrite, or
resolution of either selected research task is established by this document.
The machine must construct and test the machinery and supply the corresponding
evidence. A general continuation theorem, a useful research result, and a full
executable Gödel switch are separate achievements with separate obligations.

The absence of inherited answers does not establish historical originality:
claims of novelty still require a literature audit. Failed searches, timeouts,
and unfinished formalizations remain incomplete work, not evidence that the
mathematical target is false or unprovable.

The four unchanged modules retain their previously verified builds;\nthe new Indices module was independently compiled here. All 48 named theorems\nhave only propext, Classical.choice, and\nQuot.sound in their axiom closures. Exact snapshots, hashes, compilation output,\nand axiom output are recorded in report.json. No active source was edited and\nno mathematical proof hint was supplied to the proposer.\n\n## Family and target definitions\n\nBiPoly is a polynomial in u with integer-polynomial coefficients in v.\nThe coefficient function therefore returns the ordinary integer coefficient\nof u^i v^j. The seeds and both recurrence orientations match the source\nnumerator recurrence specialized at w=1. The previous independent scan audit\nseparately verified the exact original Laurent mutation on its finite family.\n\nInPolygon is the stated polygon in natural indices, with nonnegativity supplied\nby their type. WeakLC covers every consecutive horizontal, vertical, and\nconstant-i+j triple without subtracting natural indices or omitting zeros.\nConjecture63 is explicitly a proposition definition, not a theorem. It contains\nboth endpoints and all finite generated middle labels. The 0/1 polygon reduces\nto its singleton and the 1/1 polygon has only two lattice points, as intended.\nGeneral path/fraction completeness and recurrence/source identification are\nnot silently proved by these definitions.\n\n## Strong sequence invariant and smoothing\n\nCrossLC demands all cross inequalities f(i)f(j+1)<=f(i+1)f(j) for i<=j.\nIt is stronger than merely adjacent log-concavity for an arbitrary sequence.\nThe file does not assume that arbitrary adjacent inequalities imply CrossLC.\nInstead it proves CrossLC for the nonnegative three-term seed under AC<=B^2.\n\nThe shift and forward-sum proofs preserve CrossLC. For distinct integer\nindices, the proof uses the four appropriate cross inequalities, including\ni+1<=j; the equal-index case is equality. There is no unjustified division by\ncoefficients and no suppressed positivity assumption. The resulting Smooth\noperator f(k)+f(k-1), and any finite Pascal iteration, preserve CrossLC.\nThe adjacent conclusion then follows by the explicit specialization i=k-1,\nj=k. Zero coefficients remain present throughout.\n\n## Exact ordinary-polynomial coefficient bridge\n\nCoeffSeq first tests whether its integer index is negative and returns zero\nthere. Only nonnegative indices are converted to natural indices. Ordinary\npolynomial coefficients also vanish past the degree. This is the correct\nzero extension, not an accidental truncation of negative indices to zero.\n\ncoeffSeq_smooth, coeffSeq_quadratic, and coeffSeq_binomial_mul identify the\nabstract sequence with the actual coefficients of (1+X)^n times the stated\nquadratic. Consequently quadratic_binomial_logConcave proves an ordinary raw\ncoefficient inequality, not a factorial-normalized substitute. Its assumptions\nare A,B,C>=0 and AC<=B^2; no real-rootedness assertion is made or needed.\n\n## Universal third-diagonal expression theorem\n\nThirdA=(a-1)(a-2)/2, ThirdB=ab-4a+2, and ThirdC=(b-1)(b-2)/2\nare exactly the coefficients in the published factored third-diagonal\nexpression. third_gap_certificate is a checked exact polynomial identity.\nthird_parameters derives nonnegativity and the quadratic coefficient\ninequality for real a>=3 and b>=a+1 by that identity and nonnegative terms.\n\nthird_diagonal_expression_logConcave therefore proves, for every pair of\nnatural numbers 3<=a<b and every integer k, the adjacent coefficient inequality\nfor\n\n    (1+X)^(a+b-5) * (ThirdA a + ThirdB a b*X + ThirdC b*X^2).\n\nThe exponent is in its ordinary-polynomial range under these hypotheses;\nnatural subtraction causes no negative-exponent truncation. No gcd or ratio\nrestriction is necessary for this explicit-polynomial theorem. It does not\ncover the a=1 and a=2 families. It proves at least weak log-concavity and does\nnot assert real-rootedness or a full two-dimensional inequality.\n\n## Scope conclusion\n\nNo mathematical error or statement mismatch was found. The two important\nbridges must remain distinct: the polynomial-to-Pascal coefficient bridge is\nproved here; the recurrence-generated Markov numerator-to-third-diagonal\nexpression bridge remains a separate formal obligation. The theorem's own\ncomment states that restriction correctly. Full Conjecture 6.3 remains open.\n\nThe boundary result, added third-diagonal transfer, and completed examples\nare covered below.\n\n\n## Added third-diagonal expression and transfer\n\nSourceThird gives the source's literal three-term polynomial expression, with\nparameter n=a+b-5. sourceThird_factor proves that it equals the quadratic-times-\nbinomial form previously audited. DiagonalSeq extends the actual raw diagonal\ncoefficient list by zero outside 0<=k<=d; it tests those bounds before natural\nsubtraction, so negative indices do not collapse onto coefficient zero.\n\nThirdDiagonalFormula is a proposition definition asserting equality of the\nactual diagonal sequence and the source expression. It is not an axiom or an\nestablished universal identity. third_diagonal_of_formula derives the raw\ninequality from this explicit hypothesis for 3<=a<b. The new code therefore\nexposes the remaining identification obligation instead of silently treating\nit as discharged. All exponents are in their ordinary-polynomial range under\nthe transfer theorem's hypotheses.\n\n## Fully connected j=0 boundary result\n\nedgeEval sets the inner polynomial variable v to zero and casts integer\ncoefficients to real coefficients. The new theorem edgeEval_coeff explicitly\nproves that its ith coefficient is the real cast of coeff P i 0. Thus no\ncoefficient specialization, orientation, or normalization bridge is missing.\n\nEdgeFormula records both denominator-label positivity and the equality\nedgeEval P = X^a (X+1)^(b-1). Its initial cases are proved. Its recurrence step\nuses positive b to kill the V^b subtraction term at v=0 and correctly combines\nthe remaining exponents. Induction covers every finite left/right path of the\nactual defined recurrence. No finite denominator bound is used and no boundary\ncoefficient identity is taken as an external assumption.\n\nThe coefficient sequence of X^a(1+X)^n is proved CrossLC using the audited\nsmoothing and shift lemmas. boundary_logConcave applies this to the generated\nboundary, and boundary_raw_logConcave transports it to the literal integer\nraw coefficients used by WeakLC:\n\n    A(i,0) A(i+2,0) <= A(i+1,0)^2\n\nfor every natural i and every finite path. This is stronger than restricting\nto polygon triples along that boundary. Positivity of label denominators makes\nthe natural exponent b-1 legitimate. No truncated-index artifact is used.\n\nThis is an unconditional universal theorem for the generated j=0 boundary.\nIt re-establishes a known boundary result in the source; it is not a solution\nof all interior lines or all directions of Conjecture 6.3. No mathematical\nerror or misleading scope claim was found in the accepted modules.\n\n\n## Completed examples and missing-condition distinctions\n\nThe left child is explicitly expanded as the 1/3 numerator. Its raw vertical\ncoefficients at (1,0),(1,1),(1,2) are proved equal to 1,2,3. The corresponding\nraw inequality is strictly satisfied, and division by the correct multinomial\nfactors 3,6,3 gives a strictly reversed inequality. Thus the normalized failure\nbelongs to the actual generated family and does not refute its raw target.\n\nBoth three-term sequences [1,2,1] and [0,2,0] satisfy CrossLC, while their\nnonnegative difference [1,0,1] fails. This correctly disproves unrestricted\nsubtraction preservation. It does not disprove the specific Markov recurrence.\n\nThe parameter pair (3,4) gives the seed 1+2X+3X^2. Both the negative\nquadratic discriminant and its coefficient inequality are proved; the separate\nstrict-positivity theorem at every real x confirms there is no real root.\nThis rules out a real-rootedness requirement for the present coefficient result,\nwithout ruling out coefficient log-concavity.\n\nThe two endpoint WeakLC assertions are vacuous because no three-point line fits\ninside their polygons. At the initial 1/2 label the only relevant three-point\nline has coefficients [1,2,1]; the code correctly proves that case while the\nother directions are vacuous. No support positions are silently removed.\n\nAll accepted example statements match these interpretations. The final six\nindex theorems are additionally audited below.\n\n\n## Final index invariant and reduced-label theorem\n\nFrameIndices records that the middle is the mediant of the two endpoints,\nthe oriented determinant is one, the endpoint denominators are positive,\nthe upper endpoint has positive numerator, and the endpoints lie within the\nstated bounds of [0,1]. These are true initially and are proved preserved by\nboth actual recurrence branches; fold induction covers every finite path.\n\ncoprime_of_det correctly derives coprimality from c*b=a*d+1: the gcd of a,b\ndivides both products, hence divides 1. frame_reduced applies this to the\nmiddle and upper labels. Its exact conclusion is 0<a<b and gcd(a,b)=1 for\nevery generated middle label. This is a soundness-of-labeling theorem. It\nasserts neither injectivity of path labeling nor surjectivity onto all reduced\nfractions. The new documentation explicitly retains general coverage as a\nformal obligation. No circular assumption about coverage or log-concavity\nenters the invariant proof.\n\nFinal mathematical source hashes all agree with the independently checked\nsnapshots. Documentation equivalence is reviewed in DOCUMENTATION_REVIEW.md.\nNo error or misleading mathematical scope claim was found in the final\naccepted five-module, 48-theorem construction.\n","sha256":"c43cd8a52bef2073f028bafcb8a793b8d2208f7924ba318257b7acfbcee45c1d"},"evidence/independent-markov/markov_residual_scope_audit.md":{"content":"# Residual experiments and transport: independent scope audit\n\nDate: 13 October 2026. Read-only mathematical review of developing machine output. No active files changed, no proof suggestions sent to the proposer, and no conjecture solved by this review.\n\n## Recorded snapshots\n\n| File | SHA256 |\n| --- | --- |\n| `evidence/markov/residuals.py` | `e23381799403a5f87ed075a8fa36831e145dfc6eb4f93357bc2defae93941fa0` |\n| `evidence/markov/residual-result.json` | `d9c7a9c9dd9e33fada40ff2e016b7b25182157cefe3ed338ae90c269ab09bffd` |\n| `evidence/markov/residual-coefficients.json` | `cd32a761833943f8ed6343869e6d176f63d37ac6080f77cd79f54a17639610c0` |\n| `evidence/markov/stress.py` | `9557e269368b339aeb944719fbc55cfed8505d225e36c6f9c27683aa86f28332` |\n| `evidence/markov/stress-result.json` | `cd261a1c994fe0a81ae14556f69022f3cf0dc81ee4cbfc7d43c2a5cffa7ca2be` |\n| `evidence/markov/response-0006.json` | `efa75376881a4e643a3ddf335ed88c2ae27620092e4a66583c4499e816b9346d` |\n| `MathGKM/MarkovLogConcavity.lean` | `458b5ff6169b3f09ceaed75a31f213a202257874620bda185a3752401a7a69a6` |\n\n## Exact residual meaning\n\nFor a generated numerator of degree d=a+b\u22121, the script forms, for each integer 0\u2264r\u2264d,\n\n\\[\nT_r(t)=\\sum_{k=0}^{d-r} A_{k,d-r-k}t^k,\n\\qquad m_r=\\max(d-2r,0).\n\\]\n\nThus r is the exponent of the omitted homogeneous variable w. The script attempts exact division by `(1+t)^m_r` and tests the resulting coefficient list. No variable-dependent coefficient normalization is performed.\n\nThe exponent is a prescribed nonnegative integer. It is **not** a measurement of the largest possible power dividing the diagonal polynomial. For r=2 it agrees with a+b\u22125 when that number is nonnegative. For 2r\u2265d there is no division, so the residual is the original diagonal polynomial. These cases remain in the scan.\n\nThe intended universal residual claim should include existence of an integer-polynomial quotient Q satisfying `T_r=(1+t)^m_r Q`, followed by its coefficient properties. A theorem merely conditional on divisibility would be weaker than the experimentally tested combined claim. The current prose's \u201cafter exact removal\u201d presupposes this existence; it is not yet a formal definition.\n\nThe division code is mathematically exact: for ascending coefficients c\u2080,\u2026,c\u2099, it constructs q\u2080=c\u2080 and q\u2096=c\u2096\u2212q\u2096\u208b\u2081, then checks c\u2099=q\u2099\u208b\u2081. That is the coefficient identity for multiplication by 1+t. Repeating a verified step tests the stated power. Integer arithmetic is used throughout. A failure is recorded before further division; none is reported in either inspected result.\n\nThe lists retain leading, trailing and internal zeros. Zero diagonals are included and remain zero after division. The original list length and the bound on m prevent requesting division of a list with fewer than two positions. If division succeeds, the residual degree is at most min(r,d\u2212r); the list need not have a nonzero coefficient in its final position.\n\n## Tested predicate versus the Lean transport hypothesis\n\nBoth scripts test only:\n\n\\[\nq_k\\ge0,\\qquad q_k^2\\ge q_{k-1}q_{k+1}\n\\quad(1\\le k<\\text{list length}-1).\n\\]\n\nThey do not directly test all cross inequalities from the Lean definition\n\n\\[\n\\operatorname{CrossLC}(q):\\quad\nq_iq_{j+1}\\le q_{i+1}q_j\\quad\\text{for every }i\\le j,\n\\]\n\nwith zero extension outside the finite list. These predicates cannot be silently identified when zeros are allowed. Nonnegative adjacent log-concavity alone permits separated positive blocks; it does not supply the current Lean transport's hypothesis. Consequently the present residual conjecture, as worded, does not automatically imply the original diagonal inequalities by the proved `CrossLC` transport. A relation between the precise conjectured predicate and that hypothesis remains an explicit mathematical obligation.\n\nThis is a gap in a possible implication claim, not a counterexample to the residual conjecture or to Markov log-concavity. The reviewed response-0006 does not assert that the implication has been proved; it expressly limits the residual conjecture to one direction.\n\nAs an independent audit of the **saved denominator\u226416 data only**, I checked the finite lists for internal zero gaps and the cross inequalities. Among 1,293 saved lists, 431 were identically zero; none had an internal gap between positive entries, and no cross-inequality failure occurred. This is an auditor's additional finite validation of those saved lists, not a machine-authored theorem, not a universal bridge, and not a verification of the unsaved 6,822 stress-test residual lists. It must not be attributed to the machine's original adjacent-only test.\n\nThe phrase \u201cresidual positivity\u201d in response-0006 is loose: the code checks nonnegativity, and many lists are identically zero. The actual conjecture statement correctly says \u201cnonnegative\u201d. Strict positivity would contradict the recorded data.\n\n## Finite evidence actually recorded\n\nThe first residual run uses the earlier 79 fractions with denominator at most 16. It reports 1,293 diagonal lists, no failed divisions, no negative residual coefficients and no failed adjacent inequalities. It also separately checks 2,018 critical-triangle coefficients for divisibility by 4.\n\nThe stress run reports:\n\n| Quantity | Recorded count |\n| --- | ---: |\n| Reduced interior fractions, denominator\u226428 | 241 |\n| Original raw coefficient triples in all three principal directions | 229,476 |\n| Upper-diagonal residual lists | 6,822 |\n| Critical-triangle coefficients | 20,781 |\n\nNo failures are recorded. There are no equality examples among the tested valid raw triples, which is finite evidence only; it is not a universal strict-log-concavity theorem. The stress file correctly labels its result \u201cfinite exact computation only\u201d. Its six displayed 17/28 residuals are examples, not a complete replacement for the omitted full residual dataset.\n\nThis review read the scripts and inspected their saved results. Apart from the explicitly identified audit of saved residual lists, it did not rerun the original experiments or independently certify every reported stress-test computation.\n\n## Separate mathematical targets\n\n1. **Published Conjecture 6.3:** the raw coefficients are log-concave along all three principal directions, on every source polynomial. The raw finite scan tests that predicate on a finite denominator range.\n2. **Machine-selected residual conjecture:** exact prescribed-factor divisibility and nonnegative adjacent-log-concave residual coefficients on all upper diagonals. It is unproved, concerns only the constant-i+j direction, and has the transport issue above. Calling it \u201cstronger\u201d should not imply that it already entails all of Conjecture 6.3 or that its novelty has been established by a literature survey.\n3. **Published factor-4 conjecture:** source Conjecture 8.1 requires `4 \u2223 A_ij` when `i<a`, `j<b`, and `bi+aj>ab`. The scripts use exactly these strict conditions. This is an independent arithmetic property, not a consequence established by either log-concavity experiment. [Primary source \u00a78](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html).\n4. **Current third-diagonal Lean result:** the file proves an algebraic factorization of `SourceThird`, and states transport from the explicit assumption `ThirdDiagonalFormula l`. That assumption is a `Prop` definition, not an added axiom or a theorem already identifying every generated row. The current result remains conditional on this bridge for actual Markov coefficients.\n\nThe factor 4 in the separate polynomial gap certificate merely clears denominators. It must not be conflated with Conjecture 8.1's divisibility-by-4 assertion about critical-triangle coefficients.\n\n## Acceptance conclusion\n\nThe experiments are meaningful finite tests and distinguish the named conjectures appropriately. No claim resolving full Conjecture 6.3 was found in the reviewed decisions or theorem comments. The substantive correction needed before any future implication claim is to keep adjacent residual log-concavity distinct from the `CrossLC` premise, particularly in the presence of zeros. Formal divisibility, full family coverage, the actual coefficient identification and the two remaining directions are separate unresolved obligations.\n","sha256":"6cb707622a6c57fb2b8ac5167b302b5c21daafe5ac332b223b137407db874e35"},"evidence/independent-markov/markov_round5_target_definition_audit.md":{"content":"# Round 5 Markov target definition audit\n\nDate: 13 October 2026. Scope: mathematical meaning of the newly written target, not a proof of the conjecture. Read-only review; no active-project edits, retired material, or proof-search advice.\n\nSnapshots reviewed:\n\n- `/Users/sasha/math_gkm/MathGKM/Markov.lean`, 58 lines, SHA256 `45904bfcef813a7b14369c824f5b7435d2fbc58ab0380dafd27ab2fc2bd3ce9f`.\n- `/Users/sasha/math_gkm/evidence/markov/source-audit.md`, SHA256 `97e90023b52fffc3d8ae35aebfdcd6a61e8b2298aece39a0960828653bc136bd`.\n\nReference: [Evans\u2013Veselov\u2013Winn, published source](https://armj.math.stonybrook.edu/Articles/250708-Winn/index.html), equations (5), (7)\u2013(11), Definitions 6.1\u20136.2, Conjecture 6.3; also the earlier independent `/private/tmp/math_gkm_godel_20261013/markov_target_status_audit.md`.\n\n**Finding:** no actual English/Lean mismatch was found in these target definitions. Their mathematical interpretation matches the intended conjecture, subject to the family-identification and coverage bridges listed below. No theorem proving `Conjecture63` occurs in this snapshot. The source prose correctly calls the indexing correspondence mathematically audited, not yet proved in Lean.\n\n## Representation and normalization\n\nLines 9\u201313 use `Polynomial (Polynomial \u2124)`: the outer variable `U` is u, the coefficient-ring variable `V` is v. Consequently `(P.coeff i).coeff j` extracts the unscaled coefficient of u^i v^j. There is no factorial/binomial renormalization, parameter evaluation at u=v=1, or summation over a row.\n\nSetting w=1 is appropriate for the source homogeneous numerator: degree d fixes the omitted exponent as d\u2212i\u2212j. This is the interpretation of this representation, not a homogeneity theorem already present in the Lean file. Using \u2124 allows subtraction in the recurrence; it does not add a signed-polynomial hypothesis to the conjecture, which quantifies only over generated polynomials.\n\nLine 26 supplies the correct normalized seed numerators: 1 at 0/1, `(U+V)^2+U` at 1/2, and `U+V` at 1/1. In particular the additional term for 1/2 is U, not V. These agree with the source after w=1.\n\n## Path coverage and recurrence\n\n`frame` quantifies over arbitrary finite Boolean lists, not a fixed depth or a single repeated-branch family. The empty list includes 1/2. The two branches give middle labels 1/3 and 2/3 at the first step; both endpoints are separately included in `Conjecture63`.\n\nMathematically these are the usual binary Farey refinements on [0,1]. With frame endpoints a/b and c/d and middle (a+c)/(b+d), the right branch has middle (a+2c)/(b+2d), and the left branch (2a+c)/(2b+d). The associated polynomial expressions in lines 31 and 34 match equation (8) and its exchanged-endpoint form, respectively, after w=1. The subtracted polynomial is the opposite endpoint, and its monomial uses the retained endpoint's exponents. No branch/index swap was found.\n\n`Label` and `Frame` themselves have no validity conditions. This causes no scope enlargement in `Conjecture63`: it uses only `frame path`, which starts at `initial`. A future theorem for arbitrary frames would require its own hypotheses, but that is not the current statement.\n\n## Polygon, directions, zeros and endpoints\n\nLines 38\u201339 use the source polygon inequality after clearing positive denominators: `a*b \u2264 b*i+a*j`, and the upper bound `i+j \u2264 a+b\u22121`. Natural indices supply i,j\u22650. For actual positive-slope labels the subtraction by one is exact. At 0/1 the same formula gives i+j\u22640, hence the singleton (0,0); it does not attempt to encode the Laurent factor x^(\u22121) using natural subtraction.\n\nThe three conjuncts of `WeakLC` test precisely these consecutive triples:\n\n- `(i,j), (i+1,j), (i+2,j)`;\n- `(i,j), (i,j+1), (i,j+2)`;\n- `(i,j+2), (i+1,j+1), (i+2,j)`.\n\nTheir centers and neighbors correspond to directions (1,0), (0,1), (1,\u22121). Natural starting indices omit no valid triple inside the first quadrant. Reversing a direction gives the same inequality. In particular the third conjunct is the constant-i+j diagonal, not the increasing-i+j diagonal.\n\nEvery triple is guarded by polygon membership for all three positions. Coefficient zero is not filtered out, so internal missing coefficients remain tested. All inequalities are non-strict and compare the center square with the product of its two neighbors. Boundary positions without two neighbors impose no inequality. The 0/1 singleton and the two lattice positions at 1/1 are therefore correctly vacuous cases.\n\n## Outstanding formal bridges, not discovered mismatches\n\nThe current file defines the following obligations but does not contain theorems establishing them:\n\n1. Reachable labels have the intended positivity, coprimality and Farey relations, and every interior reduced rational has a path.\n2. The path-generated integer polynomial is the corresponding source normalized numerator at w=1, including the degree interpretation that makes coefficient extraction lossless.\n3. The displayed polygon formula agrees with the Newton polygon of that numerator.\n4. If the final claim is expressed for every mutation-generated Laurent polynomial rather than the paper's [0,1] representatives, the variable-permutation identification preserves the coefficient predicate.\n\nThese are statement-identification bridges. Their absence does not make the draft target wrong or prevent useful experiments. It does mean that proving a property of the recursive objects, by itself, should not be described as an end-to-end Lean formalization of the paper before the adopted bridge is made explicit. External source theorems may be recorded as external contracts if that is the campaign's declared boundary; they should not be silently treated as existing Lean theorems.\n\n## Claims audit\n\n`Conjecture63` at lines 54\u201356 is a definition of a proposition. The file contains no proof of that proposition and makes no theorem claim for its instances. The doc comment says this explicitly.\n\nThe accompanying source audit correctly identifies the raw coefficients, the three directions, the endpoint, the missing Lean coverage theorem, and the distinction between the 2026 saturation result and coefficient log-concavity. Its proposed experiments do not assert a new mathematical result. No factual correction is needed for the two reviewed snapshots on the requested target-definition issues.\n\nThis review did not run a Lean build or use numerical tests as proof evidence. # Clean bootstrap of a Gödel machine for mathematical research

This document is a design specification for a fresh construction. It supplies
no previous implementation, mathematical results, proof scripts, or successful
research strategies. It distinguishes an adaptive mathematical researcher, a
formally certified continuation model, and an executable Gödel machine. A
checked theorem about an abstract model does not by itself establish that an
implementation realizes that model or that the model describes future Astra
calls.

The intended system uses a flexible LLM proposer, reusable mathematical
components, and explicit gluing interfaces. It can search literature, conduct
computational experiments, change representations, formulate conjectures, and
attempt proofs and refutations. Its scientific objective is problem-specific.
Kolmogorov-style measurements are audit data, not a universal objective or an
automatic curiosity reward.

## What the original construction requires

Schmidhuber's target compares a proposed switch with continuing the entire
incumbent program, including future proof search and later self-modifications.
The machine and environment are axiomatized. Checking and installation take
time; the switch protocol binds a target time and can reject a late proof.
The resulting optimality claim is relative to the utility, assumptions, and
incumbent search, rather than an oracle maximum over all programs. The paper
also permits a nondegradation target, different initial searchers, and changes
to utility code justified by the previous utility. Its mathematical example
rewards the first verified proof or disproof by the reciprocal of elapsed time.
Useful changes may be unprovable in the chosen system or undiscoverable within
available resources. These requirements come from §§2.4, 3.2, 4, 5, and 6 of
[the original paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/cs/0309048).

The architecture and acceptance criteria below are our engineering proposal.
They are not claims that the original paper supplies a working implementation
for Lean, an opaque external LLM, or this mathematical research problem.

## The problem contract, rather than manufactured levels

ARC supplies an external environment with explicit levels and validated
completion conditions. The mathematics application has no corresponding
natural sequence of levels. Numbering accepted lemmas does not create one.

A run therefore starts with an explicit, versioned problem contract:

- An exact root proposition, its intended English meaning, and permitted
  assumptions. Resolution may mean a checked proof or checked negation.
- A declared utility or preference over research outcomes and their costs.
  This is supplied for the problem, not inferred from a theorem counter.
- Resource limits and a cost interpretation: abstract computation steps,
  elapsed time, provider usage, or separately recorded quantities.
- The environment assumptions under which prospective comparisons are made.
- Admission and completion rules that a proposal cannot redefine.

A root-resolution/time objective is one reasonable instance, not a default
definition of all mathematical value. Intermediate results can have value
when the contract says how that value is assessed. If such an assessment is
human or heuristic, its status must remain visible.

Truth, relevance, novelty, and expected usefulness are separate properties.
A kernel-checked lemma establishes its proposition. A separately checked
reduction can establish its logical connection to the root. Neither fact
alone establishes historical novelty or how likely the lemma is to help.
Even an implication into the root can have an impossible antecedent.
Experimental evidence may change the agenda without closing a formal task.

No part of admission, root closure, scheduling, or persistent rewrite approval
may quietly depend on source length, compression ratio, or a claimed estimate
of Kolmogorov complexity. Audit measurements can still describe reuse and
representation costs. Their production must have ordinary resource accounting.

## Open research actions and explicit evidence

The proposer needs an extensible action interface rather than a fixed menu of
prewritten mathematical recipes. Concrete capabilities can include:

| Action | Output | What the output establishes |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Literature search and source reading | Queries, primary URLs, passages, retrieval times | What a source reports; not a Lean theorem |
| Python, Sage, or GAP experiment | Program, inputs, versions, outputs, costs | A reproducible computation under recorded semantics |
| Representation proposal | Definitions, maps, examples, desired transport laws | A proposed viewpoint until its laws are checked |
| Proof or refutation | Exact target, proof term, dependencies, kernel receipt | The proposition admitted by the proof gate |
| Component attachment | Boundary, bindings, adapters, checked obligations | The specific preservation properties proved |
| Search strategy proposal | Diagnosis, next actions, resource allocation | Provisional guidance consumed by the controller |
| Persistent code rewrite | Exact replacement, state migration, switch certificate | Only the certified comparison and preservation claims |

An adapter may expose a new experimental language or mathematical interface
without giving the proposer unrestricted host authority. The broker enforces
capabilities and records failures. An unavailable Sage or GAP installation is
a capability failure, not evidence against a conjecture. Network failures,
timeouts, and malformed responses similarly remain transport or execution
outcomes rather than mathematical refutations.

Finite scans do not prove universal claims. Exact counterexamples can become
formal refutations after the relevant witness and hypotheses are independently
checked. External theorems may be recorded as explicit assumptions when a
contract permits that treatment; retrieved text must not add hidden axioms.

## Exploration must not require a switch proof at every step

The incumbent research policy may already authorize broad exploratory actions,
task invention, hypothesis changes recorded as new tasks, and provisional
strategy updates. Choosing such an action is ordinary execution of that policy.
It need not first prove that its next web query or experiment is globally best.

A persistent replacement of the controller or its search procedure is a
different event. It requires either the full switch gate described below or an
explicitly labeled experimental branch that makes no certified-improvement
claim. Successful tests alone must not promote that branch to a proved switch.

This separation prevents two failures: an inert system unable to explore until
it has solved its own research problem, and an unrestricted self-editor whose
ordinary strategy changes are advertised as Gödel-certified improvements.
Exploration remains flexible within the current contract and capability limits.

## Operational semantics and the whole continuation

The formal machine state should contain executable controller and proof-search
code, persistent research data, the archive and agenda, resource state, pending
requests, and enough environment history to interpret future actions. Program
code must be inspectable data. A semantics must explain how each instruction,
external response, and accepted rewrite changes that state.

Crucially, the incumbent continuation includes its own future proposals,
verification attempts, discoveries, and switches. A comparison against a
frozen policy that is forbidden to improve does not compare against the actual
incumbent. The replacement continuation must likewise include its subsequent
behavior, not just its first apparently beneficial action.

One conceptual interface is:

```text
step       : Program × State × Input -> Transition
run        : Program × State × Environment -> Trace
evaluate   : ProblemContract × Trace -> Utility
install    : Candidate × State -> InstallationTrace × State
```

This interface is a specification sketch, not an executable API or a proof.
In a stochastic instance, `run` induces a distribution and `evaluate` supplies
an expected value when the required measurability and integrability hold.
In a robust instance, comparisons quantify over declared environment behaviors.
The implementation must connect these objects to the bytes it actually runs.

## The switch obligation and a common time baseline

For contract `C`, model `mu`, incumbent `p`, candidate `q`, and decision state
`s`, the intended strict obligation is:

```text
V(C, mu, install-and-continue(q, s))
  > V(C, mu, continue-whole-machine(p, s)).
```

Both sides use the same contract, environmental assumptions, and decision
baseline. The comparison may instead be nonstrict when that is the declared
rule. This is a semantic statement about complete continuations; it is not a
claim that both values must be computed exactly before a proof can be found.

Search already performed before this baseline is sunk on both branches. Do not
charge it twice or selectively subtract it from the incumbent. Validation and
installation still to be performed must be included. If final validation has
already occurred, its elapsed time instead appears in the new state and the
remaining lifetime. A certificate proved from an earlier snapshot must justify
transport to the installation state or be checked against an appropriate future
deadline and invariant. Simply adding a measured cost to an old inequality is
insufficient when the remaining opportunity to solve the problem has changed.

A switch receipt must bind the contract and model, incumbent and replacement
code, exact state or proved state invariant, migration, cost interpretation,
deadline, certificate target, and independent verification artifacts. Reject
changed bindings and stale deadlines. Hashes bind recorded bytes; they are not
proofs that Python or operating-system execution realizes the Lean semantics.

Changing runtime reward code cannot redefine the standard used to approve the
change. Representation changes to the objective require a transport proof.
A new scientific objective requires a new explicit contract; silently weakening
the root or environmental assumptions is not an improvement.

## Opaque models and self-reference

Astra is an external proposer with unknown internals and no assumed success
probability. Treat its responses and delays as environmental inputs. A measured
acceptance rate, benchmark gain, or confidence estimate does not establish its
future response law. A Bayesian comparison is conditional on its declared
model; a robust comparison must actually quantify over the stated model class.
Neither should be reported as an unconditional real-world guarantee.

One promising certificate pattern proves preservation for every corresponding
response stream while reducing internal work. However, corresponding streams
require justification: an API or web service can depend on request time and
history. Faster execution need not receive the same responses. The environment
contract or a coupling argument must support that correspondence.

Encoding one's own code is not the same as proving unrestricted soundness of
one's own proof system. A sufficiently strong consistent theory cannot simply
adopt its own unrestricted reflection principle. This is the relevant obstacle
discussed in [Yudkowsky and Herreshoff's primary analysis](https://intelligence.org/files/TilingAgentsDraft.pdf).
Our design uses particular checked proofs and concrete simulations; it must
not introduce an unchecked `SelfSound` axiom to discharge future correctness.
The reference kernel, admission semantics, and runtime bridge are explicit
trust boundaries. Faster implementations need preservation certificates against
that reference; replacing the reference by a candidate's assertion of trust
does not prove preservation.

## Gluing and representation transport

A finite-name attachment can have a unique-extension property for compatible
maps. Proving such a restricted pushout would not establish semantic
conservativity of arbitrary source edits or dependent Lean declarations.

The design requires typed interfaces: declarations, hypotheses, dependencies,
interpretations, and any renaming or substitution. A new cell must discharge
its assumptions from the accepted context. Context attachment should preserve
the original models and hence their consequences. Sequential attachment must
preserve this fact, including when later cells reuse earlier checked cells.

A representation adapter must preserve the observations or predicates needed
by its consumer. When a representation identifies two objects that a target
property distinguishes, no exact adapter can recover that property from the
representation alone. Such collisions should become explicit failed obligations
or counterexamples, not be hidden by successful tests on a small sample.

For code components, coherent signatures are only the beginning: a simulation
must connect glued implementations to their specification and cost model.
Gluing correctness then supports a switch proof; it does not imply usefulness.
The terms “cofibered” and “cofibrant” require a specified category, structure,
and associated laws. Fiber-respecting maps and injective context embeddings
alone do not establish a model-category cofibration or a Grothendieck opfibration.

## Milestones and acceptance criteria

1. **Problem-directed exploration.** Run the configurable contract and action
   broker with Astra proposals, real feedback, explicit evidence classes, and
   cost accounting. Demonstrate a nonproof action affecting a later research
   decision. Synthetic fixtures test the protocol; they do not demonstrate
   autonomous mathematical discovery.
2. **Semantic foundations.** Prove conservative context attachment, representation
   transport conditions, and continuation comparisons with explicit costs.
   A bounded trace/Bellman model is a useful verified instance. State exactly
   which horizon, response relation, and policy class it quantifies over.
3. **Reflective executable bridge.** Provide executable code semantics with code
   in state and future switching included. Prove or explicitly audit the bridge
   from concrete controller transitions, time accounting, and state migration
   to that semantics. Merely supplying an arbitrary value function fails this
   milestone. A finite table or a single prescribed trajectory also fails it.
4. **A concrete certified self-change.** Produce a candidate, an independently
   checked whole-continuation certificate, and an actual guarded installation.
   A semantics-preserving optimization with a net cost improvement is a useful
   first case. Its proof must cover future switches and installation overhead,
   not merely reproduce the outcomes in the selection benchmark.
5. **General search and reuse.** Let the proposer invent components, adapters,
   and candidate rewrites. A fair proof enumerator can supply completeness
   relative to a calculus if required; an LLM alone supplies no such guarantee.
   Neither option requires a Kolmogorov reward or manufactured task levels.

Completing a finite, specified instance does not establish a switch guarantee
for arbitrary unbounded research or an unmodeled LLM. A generic theorem whose
hypotheses assume the very utility comparison at issue is a framework, not an
independent proof that a concrete rewrite improves the researcher.

## Adversarial examples and regression requirements

The audit must include passing examples and failures with one condition removed:

- A valid reduction versus an unrelated true lemma falsely credited as root
  completion; a refutation of the exact goal versus a changed-hypothesis target.
- A numerical pattern versus a kernel-checked universal statement; a missing
  experimental tool versus a negative mathematical result.
- A compatible attachment versus a conflicting binding, new unproved assumption,
  omitted dependency, circular cell dependency, or lossy representation adapter.
- A cheaper equivalent continuation versus one whose installation overhead
  removes the gain, or whose earlier deadline defeats the promised outcome.
- A full incumbent that later finds a better rewrite versus a comparator that
  artificially disables that future search; the latter certificate must fail.
- Identical objective semantics versus a replacement that edits the reward,
  root, model assumptions, or verifier to manufacture apparent improvement.
- A correctly bound certificate versus changed candidate bytes, changed state,
  stale time, mismatched model, forged receipt, or replayed old approval.
- An exploratory strategy revision versus a persistent executable rewrite;
  exploratory authorization must not silently authorize the latter.
- Different complexity-audit values with identical research inputs: admission,
  scheduling, and switch decisions remain identical. Logging costs may differ
  only when the measurement operation itself genuinely differs.

Formal negative examples should exhibit the missing mathematical hypothesis,
not just malformed JSON. Runtime tests should exercise actual gate boundaries.
Successful tests are evidence about implementation behavior, not a substitute
for the semantic connection required by milestone 3.

## Machine-authored bootstrap and experimental status

The initial input is this design, the user-selected research problem descriptions
and primary-source references, pinned Lean/Mathlib metadata, and a minimal launch
and containment interface. The machine must create the new implementation,
formal statements, proofs, experiments, tests, and documentation. The supervisor
provides execution, resource limits, evidence retention, and independent audit;
it must not insert mathematical solution steps or implement the research engine
on the machine's behalf while describing the result as machine-authored.

A bootstrap cannot claim that its first controller edits are already authorized
by a Gödel switch theorem whose verifier and executable semantics it has yet to
construct. Those edits run in an explicitly experimental workspace under the
user's authorization to rebuild. Compilation, tests, and subsequent independent
checks can validate aspects of the resulting code. They do not retroactively
prove that the bootstrap's sequence of edits was utility-optimal.

The machine must report separate transitions between these statuses:

- **Experimental bootstrap:** code generation and exploration without an
  installed whole-continuation switch certificate.
- **Checked research:** concrete proof objects pass an independently validated
  admission boundary; individual accepted propositions may be reported exactly.
- **Verified model:** formal theorems describe an explicitly stated machine and
  environment model, with the implementation bridge still separately identified.
- **Certified persistent switch:** an actual installation passes the bound,
  independently checked certificate and execution-bridge obligations above.

These labels are evidence classes, not mathematical levels, utility scores,
or a requirement that all components progress in a fixed order. A machine can
produce a valid mathematical theorem during an experimental bootstrap. That
alone certifies neither its surrounding engine nor its future self-modifications.
Machine-generated reports of success remain claims until their evidence is
independently checked; a self-authored test harness cannot certify itself by
printing a successful receipt.

## Clean-input and provenance acceptance checklist

Before the rebuilding proposer runs, independently verify the following:

- Historical source, draft implementations, proof scripts, discoveries, tests,
  experiments, transcripts, and run receipts are archived for the user outside
  the proposer's readable filesystem boundary. They are not bootstrap inputs.
- A Git archive preserves the historical work without exposing its object store
  or archive branch to the proposer. Deleting the working tree while leaving
  `git show` access to earlier solutions does not establish a clean boundary.
- No historical project `.olean`, generated module, cached proof expression,
  database, notebook output, or task-specific package supplies previous results.
  A pinned standard Lean/Mathlib installation is a declared dependency, not
  evidence of a newly created theorem.
- The proposer begins with a fresh conversation. Old assistant summaries,
  hidden solution files, previous success reports, and strategy suggestions
  are not inherited through its prompt, tools, environment, or resume state.
- Task inputs identify the selected publication or conjecture and the required
  outcome. They do not include previously found witnesses, lemmas, reductions,
  or successful representations. Public primary sources remain legitimate
  research inputs and their actual use is recorded.
- The run records an input manifest, hashes, toolchain pins, capabilities,
  workspace boundary, initial prompt, model identity, and resource limits.
  Archived historical objects and fresh generated objects remain distinguishable.
- All new code and mathematical artifacts are traceable to machine actions.
  Any later human correction, imported result, or boundary exception is recorded
  explicitly and narrows the corresponding autonomy or clean-input claim.
- Generated artifacts cannot overwrite supervisor-owned launch rules, hidden
  archives, independent validation tools, evidence manifests, or contract inputs.
  Proposed changes to those components remain candidates for separate review.

A prompt requesting that the proposer ignore readable historical answers is a
behavioral instruction, not enforced clean isolation. If filesystem isolation
is unavailable, report that limitation rather than claiming an enforced clean
run. The archive must remain recoverable by the user; cleaning the proposer
workspace does not authorize loss of the preserved historical work.

## What this specification does not yet establish

No implementation, kernel-checked result, certified controller rewrite, or
resolution of either selected research task is established by this document.
The machine must construct and test the machinery and supply the corresponding
evidence. A general continuation theorem, a useful research result, and a full
executable Gödel switch are separate achievements with separate obligations.

The absence of inherited answers does not establish historical originality:
claims of novelty still require a literature audit. Failed searches, timeouts,
and unfinished formalizations remain incomplete work, not evidence that the
mathematical target is false or unprovable.

## Exact residual meaning

For a generated numerator of degree d=a+b−1, the script forms, for each integer 0≤r≤d,

\[
T_r(t)=\sum_{k=0}^{d-r} A_{k,d-r-k}t^k,
\qquad m_r=\max(d-2r,0).
\]

Thus r is the exponent of the omitted homogeneous variable w. The script attempts exact division by `(1+t)^m_r` and tests the resulting coefficient list. No variable-dependent coefficient normalization is performed.

The exponent is a prescribed nonnegative integer. It is **not** a measurement of the largest possible power dividing the diagonal polynomial. For r=2 it agrees with a+b−5 when that number is nonnegative. For 2r≥d there is no division, so the residual is the original diagonal polynomial. These cases remain in the scan.

The intended universal residual claim should include existence of an integer-polynomial quotient Q satisfying `T_r=(1+t)^m_r Q`, followed by its coefficient properties. A theorem merely conditional on divisibility would be weaker than the experimentally tested combined claim. The current prose's “after exact removal” presupposes this existence; it is not yet a formal definition.

The division code is mathematically exact: for ascending coefficients c₀,…,cₙ, it constructs q₀=c₀ and qₖ=cₖ−qₖ₋₁, then checks cₙ=qₙ₋₁. That is the coefficient identity for multiplication by 1+t. Repeating a verified step tests the stated power. Integer arithmetic is used throughout. A failure is recorded before further division; none is reported in either inspected result.

The lists retain leading, trailing and internal zeros. Zero diagonals are included and remain zero after division. The original list length and the bound on m prevent requesting division of a list with fewer than two positions. If division succeeds, the residual degree is at most min(r,d−r); the list need not have a nonzero coefficient in its final position.

/-! Raw squared-variable numerator coefficients for Evans--Veselov--Winn 6.3.
The outer polynomial variable is u=x², the inner one v=y²; w=z² is set to 1.
Homogeneity recovers its exponent a+b-1-i-j. No factorial normalization.
-/
namespace MathGKM.Markov

noncomputable section

abbrev BiPoly := Polynomial (Polynomial ℤ)
def U : BiPoly := Polynomial.X
def V : BiPoly := Polynomial.C Polynomial.X
def S : BiPoly := U + V + 1
def coeff (P : BiPoly) (i j : ℕ) : ℤ := (P.coeff i).coeff j

structure Label where
  a : ℕ
  b : ℕ
  p : BiPoly

structure Frame where
  lo : Label
  mid : Label
  hi : Label

def initial : Frame :=
  ⟨⟨0, 1, 1⟩, ⟨1, 2, (U + V)^2 + U⟩, ⟨1, 1, U + V⟩⟩

def advance (f : Frame) (right : Bool) : Frame :=
  if right then
    ⟨f.mid, ⟨f.mid.a + f.hi.a, f.mid.b + f.hi.b,
      S * f.hi.p * f.mid.p - U^f.hi.a * V^f.hi.b * f.lo.p⟩, f.hi⟩
  else
    ⟨f.lo, ⟨f.lo.a + f.mid.a, f.lo.b + f.mid.b,
      S * f.lo.p * f.mid.p - U^f.lo.a * V^f.lo.b * f.hi.p⟩, f.mid⟩

def frame (path : List Bool) : Frame := path.foldl advance initial

def InPolygon (a b i j : ℕ) : Prop :=
  a * b ≤ b * i + a * j ∧ i + j ≤ a + b - 1

def WeakLC (a b : ℕ) (P : BiPoly) : Prop :=
  (∀ i j, InPolygon a b i j → InPolygon a b (i+1) j →
    InPolygon a b (i+2) j →
    coeff P i j * coeff P (i+2) j ≤ coeff P (i+1) j ^ 2) ∧
  (∀ i j, InPolygon a b i j → InPolygon a b i (j+1) →
    InPolygon a b i (j+2) →
    coeff P i j * coeff P i (j+2) ≤ coeff P i (j+1) ^ 2) ∧
  (∀ i j, InPolygon a b i (j+2) → InPolygon a b (i+1) (j+1) →
    InPolygon a b (i+2) j →
    coeff P i (j+2) * coeff P (i+2) j ≤ coeff P (i+1) (j+1) ^ 2)

/-- Full path-indexed target, not asserted as a theorem. The initial endpoint
0/1 has P=1 and a singleton polygon; 1/1 has P=u+v. -/
def Conjecture63 : Prop :=
  WeakLC 0 1 1 ∧ WeakLC 1 1 (U+V) ∧
  ∀ path, let m := (frame path).mid; WeakLC m.a m.b m.p

end
end MathGKM.Markov
